evidence.snippet: To our knowledge, this is the first report of a pathogenic mutation in a human nuclear encoded ATPase assembly gene.

nodes.description: The only reported disease-causing ATPAF2 allele, homozygous in the index patient from a consanguineous family. The substitution replaces a conserved neutral tryptophan with a basic arginine; in the yeast model it renders the human protein insoluble rather than altering its charge environment, implicating a change in the protein's dynamic properties.

evidence.reference_title: Variability of Clinical Phenotypes Caused by Isolated Defects of Mitochondrial ATP Synthase.
evidence.snippet: A homozygous c.280T>A substitution in ATPAF2 gene was found in a girl with dysmorphic features, cortical- subcortical brain atrophy followed by basal ganglia atrophy and metabolic acidosis, who died at the age of 14 months.

evidence.snippet: The W94R mutation alters the protein at the most highly conserved position in the Pfam sequence and renders HuAtp12p insoluble in the background of Deltaatp12.

nodes.description: ATPAF2/Atp12 binds the F1 alpha subunit and prevents nonproductive alpha/beta aggregation during formation of the catalytic alpha3-beta3 hexamer. The W94R substitution destroys this chaperone function — in the humanized yeast system the wild-type human protein rescues an atp12 deletion while the mutant protein is insoluble — so the F1 catalytic head cannot be built.

nodes.description: Failure of aerobic ATP synthesis produces lactic acidosis with 3-methylglutaconic aciduria, and in the developing brain a progressive degeneration — cortical-subcortical atrophy followed within months by basal ganglia atrophy — with severe developmental impairment. The child died at 14 months during an intercurrent infection, consistent with the heightened vulnerability of mitochondrial disease to catabolic stress.

nodes.description: The functional proof of pathogenicity for the single human allele. A yeast atp12 deletion loses F1 assembly and respiratory growth; plasmid-borne wild-type human ATPAF2 rescues it, and the W94R mutant protein is insoluble in that background. The equivalent yeast substitution behaves differently unless the yeast-specific factor Fmc1p is also removed, so the humanized-rescue arm, not the yeast-mutant arm, is the informative comparison for the human disease.
